sermon.title: The Fifth Group, Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Continuing The Fifth Group, Pastor David G. Kincer says God’s own people can bring His correction and are destroyed for lack of knowledge, while followers of Christ have great promises of protection (Exodus 15:26, Psalm 91, Luke 10:19). Using the book of Job he teaches that Satan is the destroyer, not God, and says the wise will understand what God is doing in the last days and must turn from sin, not only pray and worship.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: the captions read “Hosea 46 and Isaiah 513” and “Psalm 78 34,” rendered Hosea 4:6, Isaiah 5:13 and Psalm 78:34. He gives “Deuteronomy 15” for “I’ll take all sicknesses from you”; that promise is Deuteronomy 7:15 (shown). He calls the parable with the tares “the parable of the sower”; the tares are in the parable of the wheat and tares (Matthew 13:38, shown). His figure that fifty percent of sexually active people in America have a sexually transmitted disease and his comments about groups and churches are his own and are not verified here. Several words are marked [unclear].

faqs.question: What do people want preachers to tell them, according to Isaiah 30:10?
faqs.answer: He says they want smooth, pleasant things: “tell us we’re all going to prosper tell us we’re all going to go to heaven no matter how we live.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Who say to the seers, “Do not see,” And to the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us right things; Speak to us smooth things, prophesy deceits.

faqs.question: Why does he say there are refugees all over the world?
faqs.answer: He says it is because governments aren’t teaching right and most of the church is so flattering that Christians have no motivation to do right.

faqs.question: Are there atheists in foxholes?
faqs.answer: He recalls a family member who fought in World War II saying everybody was praying when bullets were flying: “no atheists in foxholes.”

faqs.question: Do you have to be perfect to receive God’s promises?
faqs.answer: He says “don’t think if you have to be perfect”; if you have a goal to reach the righteousness of God, “he will bless your socks off.”

faqs.question: Is every accident God’s correction?
faqs.answer: He says if you have an accident on the freeway “just relax that’s an accident.”

faqs.question: Does he say Satan was created as the destroyer?
faqs.answer: He says God created the waster to destroy, and Satan “wasn’t an accident”; he is the tempter whose job is to try to destroy you.

faqs.question: Why did God allow Job to be tested?
faqs.answer: He says God wanted to show Satan and all of mankind that followers will follow God no matter if bad things or good things happen to them.

faqs.question: What changed the apostles for life?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus opened their understanding of the Scriptures, and coupled with the baptism of the Holy Spirit in Acts 2 it was “a one-two punch,” filling them with power to be witnesses.

faqs.question: Why does he say people don’t see the sexual revolution isn’t working?
faqs.answer: He says the Bible says the wicked don’t understand: “when your heart is wicked it is stupid.”

faqs.question: If God’s presence is in a worship service, does that mean He approves?
faqs.answer: He says if he goes to a son doing wrong, his presence is not approval; he has come to correct.

faqs.question: Can Christians be a source of change?
faqs.answer: He says we can know what’s happening in the last days, relax because of what we know, and be a source of change in this earth.
